prompt: A parking lot has $200$ cars at $t = 0$ (8 a.m.). For $0 \le t \le 8$ hours, cars enter at a rate of $E(t) = 48 - 4t$ cars per hour and leave at a rate of $L(t) = 4t$ cars per hour. What is the maximum number of cars in the lot during this period?
hint: The number of cars $N(t)$ grows while $E(t) > L(t)$ and shrinks once $L(t) > E(t)$. Find the time when the two rates are equal.

hints.text: The number of cars $N(t)$ grows while $E(t) > L(t)$ and shrinks once $L(t) > E(t)$. Find the time when the two rates are equal.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $48 - 4t = 4t$ gives $t = 6$. Before $t = 6$ the net rate $E - L = 48 - 8t$ is positive, and after it is negative. So $N$ peaks at $t = 6$ (2 p.m.).
The count at the peak is the starting count plus the net change: $N(6) = 200 + \int_0^6 (48 - 8t) \, dt = 200 + [48t - 4t^2]_0^6$. Evaluate the bracket.
The maximum number in the lot is $200 + (288 - 144) = 344$ cars.

explanation: The net rate is $N'(t) = E(t) - L(t) = 48 - 8t$. This is zero at $t = 6$, positive before and negative after, so $N$ has its maximum at $t = 6$.
Add the net change to the starting count: $N(6) = N(0) + \int_0^6 (48 - 8t) \, dt = 200 + \left[48t - 4t^2\right]_0^6 = 200 + (288 - 144)$.
That is $344$ cars at 2 p.m. Check the endpoints: $N(0) = 200$ and $N(8) = 200 + (384 - 256) = 328$, both smaller. This is the standard AP "rate in, rate out" question.
